answer: Behavioural beacon anchoring: each agent must broadcast a signed, low-entropy summary of its past-epoch action mix, and every peer keeps a rolling sketch of those summaries. A new identity is only usable once its beacon matches an established umber of prior epochs within a fixed tolerance; mismatches downgrade routing priority. Attackers must sustain many parallel identities across epochs, paying continuous compute and storage to keep each sketch coherent—roughly the cost of running one honest sonnet-writing agent per fake identity, making mass sybils economically self-defeating.
